content: Avemar, a wheat germ extract, has specific dosing recommendations based on the patient’s weight. For individuals weighing less than 90 kg, the recommended dose is 9 grams taken orally once daily. For those weighing more than 90 kg, the dose is 9 grams taken orally twice daily. The powder should be mixed in 150 mL of water or another liquid that does not contain vitamin C and consumed one hour before meals. Avemar has been studied primarily in certain cancers, particularly colorectal cancer. Small clinical trials have demonstrated significant improvements in progression-free survival and overall survival, as well as the absence of metastases in colorectal cancer patients compared to control groups. These findings were published in the British Journal of Cancer (2003) and Hepato-Gastroenterology (2000). Additional studies suggest survival benefits in melanoma patients and improvements in quality of life for breast cancer patients. Avemar is approved in Hungary as a medical nutrient. Interactions with other substances should be carefully monitored. Ascorbic acid (vitamin C) and rose hips reduce the effectiveness of wheat germ extract through an unknown mechanism. To mitigate this, the manufacturer recommends separating the administration of these substances by at least two hours. Wheat germ extract may enhance the effects of tamoxifen through pharmacodynamic synergy, which could be beneficial in estrogen receptor-positive (ER+) breast cancer. However, the clinical significance of this interaction is not fully understood, and close monitoring is advised. Adverse effects associated with Avemar include soft stools, nausea, and diarrhea. It is contraindicated in patients with malabsorption syndrome, gastrointestinal ulcers, celiac disease, gluten sensitivity, inherited fructose intolerance, hypersensitivity to the product, and those undergoing transplants. It should only be administered to patients who have been able to tolerate oral food intake without complications for at least four days. Other medicinal products or supplements, particularly those containing vitamin C, should be given at least two hours apart from Avemar. Avemar is not recommended during pregnancy or lactation. It falls under the pregnancy category avoid, as there is insufficient evidence to confirm its safety during these periods.
